title: Sulfur Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Sulfur Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Sulfur deficiency shows on the young leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Sulfur deficiency in plants starts on the young leaves and the growing tip. Sulfur is part of the amino acids cysteine and methionine, so plants need it to build proteins. It helps make chlorophyll and helps legumes form their root nodules. It is also part of the enzyme that turns nitrate into protein. So a crop short of sulfur cannot use its nitrogen well. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

blocks.text: Sulfur moves only slowly out of old leaves, so most crops show the pale color first on the young, upper leaves. A few crops, such as citrus, show it on old leaves first, and a bad shortage turns the whole plant pale.
Sulfur deficiency symptoms

Young leaves turn evenly pale green to yellow, veins included, and in bad cases the whole plant looks washed out. Plants stay short and thin with stiff, woody stems, and they ripen late. Rice makes fewer tillers and shorter panicles, and yellow seedlings in the seedbed die in large numbers after transplanting. In corn the upper leaves can show pale stripes between darker veins.
Sulfur deficiency by crop

Each crop shows it its own way. So find yours in the tables below, then open its page for the photo and the full fix, like the one for [sulfur in rice](/nutrient-deficiencies/rice-nutrient-deficiency#sulfur).

blocks.text: What causes sulfur deficiency

Sulfate washes out of sandy soils low in organic matter, the more so with heavy rain soon after planting. Highly weathered red soils rich in iron oxides, allophane volcanic soils and fields where straw is burned or hauled away also run short. Fields fed only urea and muriate of potash get no sulfur at all, because neither fertilizer contains it. PCA surveys also found sulfur short in some coconut areas.
How to be sure it is sulfur

Sulfur shortage looks almost the same as nitrogen shortage. The clue is where it starts: sulfur paleness shows on the young leaves first, while nitrogen yellows the old leaves first. Soil tests for sulfur help but are less exact than tests for phosphorus or potassium. So a leaf tissue test is the surer check. In lowland rice, the PhilRice MOET pots show if sulfur is the missing nutrient.
How to fix sulfur deficiency

Ammonium sulfate (21 0 0) is the usual fix. Gypsum, superphosphate (0 20 0), sulfate of potash and Epsom salt also supply sulfate. Elemental sulfur works only after soil bacteria turn it into sulfate, so it is slow. A typical field crop rate is 11 kg of sulfur per hectare, near one bag of ammonium sulfate, but the soil test decides.

How to keep sulfur deficiency away

Use ammonium sulfate or another sulfur carrying fertilizer in the basal dose, and plow straw back in instead of burning it. In rice, dry tillage after harvest and good drainage between crops keep more sulfur in a form roots can take.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: In flooded fields rich in organic matter, heavy sulfate can turn into hydrogen sulfide, which blackens rice roots. The young leaves then turn yellow between the veins, much like iron shortage.

blocks.text: Sulfur deficiency questions

items.q: What does sulfur deficiency look like?
items.a: The young, upper leaves turn evenly pale green or yellow, veins and all, and the plant stays short and thin. It looks like nitrogen shortage, but nitrogen starts on the old leaves.

items.q: What is the best fertilizer for sulfur deficiency?
items.a: Ammonium sulfate (21 0 0) is the usual choice because it carries both nitrogen and sulfur. Gypsum and sulfate of potash also supply sulfur, while elemental sulfur acts slowly.
No. Urea (46 0 0) and muriate of potash (0 0 60) carry no sulfur. So a field fed only these two can run short. Swap part of the urea for ammonium sulfate.

items.q: How much ammonium sulfate should I give a coconut tree?
items.a: The PCA guide gives a typical rate that rises with age, up to 1.5 kg per palm a year for palms 5 years and older. Spread it in a ring around the trunk, or in holes on sloping land. Let a soil or leaf test fine tune it.
